::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 29th [1872-1898]  
**Manuscript:** MS with Waiting For Godot Books, 2005, transcribed from Abebooks.
:::

Dear [Mrs. Bacon](people/person_89.qmd)

With many thanks I am afraid I do not see my way to being able to come to your garden party on the 6th. I am going from home the week after and there is a good deal on hand. 

Yours sincerely, 
C M Yonge.

---

**Note:** Francis Kenrick Bacon (1826/7-1886), retired major in the Bengal Staff Corps, and his wife Sarah Lucy Bacon (1835/6-?1920) are found at the Red House, Hursley, in the 1881 census.  They seem to have arrived by 1872, judging by other newspaper references, and she was still living there as a widow in the 1901 census.  The Hampshire Chronicle  (26 Nov 1887) records that he was buried in the churchyard and she gave a handsome lectern to the church in his memory.
